text:
Version control helps developers track changes to their code. Git, a popular tool for this, lets you create feature branches. A branch is a separate workspace where you can build a new feature without affecting the main codebase, usually called 'main' or 'master'. This is a core part of a modern version control workflow.

Once your feature is complete and tested, you merge it back into the main branch. In team settings, this is often done through a pull request. A pull request is not just a merge; it’s a review process. Your teammates can see, comment on, and approve your changes before they are combined. This approach reduces errors, encourages collaboration, and keeps the main code stable.
